history.p: Gade started working on "Mariotta" in the autumn of 1848 having returned from Leipzig. In a letter to Conrad Schleinitz dated 29 October 1849 he wrote: "Das Stück spielt in Italien, ich musste also aus meine nordische Nebel heraus, und es hat mich wohlgethan in vielen Hinsicht." (The piece is set in Italy which meant that I had to get out of my Nordic mist which has done me good in many ways). The Singspiel only had nine performances and was never revived. It remained Gade's only opera. Mariotta's Romance from Act One, however, became very popular.

Hil Dig! Fyrste! Kronens Smykke skal du bære til vor Lykke!

physDesc.physMedium: Full bound in black cloth with golden frame. In the middle of the front cover and on the spine in gold: "MARIOTTA, / AF / N. W. GADE". No title page. Written in ink. Paper: 20 staves. Different paginations. The overture for piano four hands. With several cancellations and emendations. Pages trimmed in connection with binding. Act One no.1 end-dated "25 October / 1848"; no. 2 "2 Novbr. 1848; no. 3 "11 Novbr. 1848"; after no. 4: "Fine dal Atto 1mo. / 8 Decbr. 1848.". A gathering inserted, paginated 1-22 with no. 5 and no. 8. At the beginning of Act Two, no. 5 has been corrected to No 7. At the end of no. 7 Gade's musical signature, but no dating. At the end of Act Two: "Fine !!! / [Gade's musical signature] / Kjøbenhavn. / October / 1849."

All three volumes full bound in green cloth with handwritten label in upper left-hand corner on the cover inscribed: "Mariotta / 1. Akt; [2. Akt]; [3. Akt]". On the spine written in ink: "428 Mariotta 1.; [2]; [3.] P."
